format: Independent motorcycle shop, scooter CVT service, column-aligned
why: The only motorcycle coverage in the set, and the class the pipeline was demonstrably worst at. A scooter's CVT service used to come back as Transmission - the closest word the car-only vocabulary offered - and Transmission is not a component a motorcycle has, so the record attributed to nothing and disappeared from the parts map entirely.

Tests the whole of F5 and F6 at once: CVT CLEANING, DRIVE BELT and WEIGHT ROLLER SET are only classifiable as Drive Chain / CVT if the extractor knows this is a motorcycle and is offered a vocabulary that contains the answer.
Also tests that a motorcycle is never given AC System, which the old shared vocabulary allowed.
All four line kinds appear: operations, parts, a material (shop towel and contact cleaner) and a fee (disposal). The GTA case has no MATERIAL or FEE, so without this one those two kinds are untested.
Column-aligned with the pipe separator, so it also exercises the layout format the OCR layer now produces. Both other cases predate layout reconstruction and arrive as prose.
Ends in Tagalog. Nothing after TOTAL is transaction content and none of it may reach any field.
redacted: n/a - no real customer data, this case is written rather than captured
notes: SYNTHETIC. Written by hand because no real motorcycle receipt was available, and a class with zero coverage was worse than a class covered by a clean example. It is clean in ways real OCR is not: no character errors, no dropped glyphs, no column drift. Treat its scores as an upper bound.
Replace it with a real motorcycle receipt when one can be photographed. Until then it proves the vocabulary and the vehicle context work; it does not prove they survive bad OCR.
Line amounts sum to 2,450.00 exactly, matching the printed total, so reconciliation is scored here too.
